To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the angiotension II (AT) receptor antagonist losartan, injected into the anterior hypothalamus, lowers blood pressure in deoxycorticosteroid (DOCA) salt hypertensive rats.
the angiotension-system in the anterior hypothalamus is enhanced in DOCA-saline hypertensive rats and that this enhancement plays an important role in the maintenance of their hypertension.
the blockade of angiotensinsin receptors in the AHA lowers blood pressure in hypertensive rats.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of angiotensins in the pathogenesis of experimental and essential hypertension.
the pathogenesis of brain angiotensins in DOCA-saline hypertensive rats.
the pathogenesis of DOCA-salt hypertension.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the blockade of angiotensins in the AHA produces a depressor response in conscious DOCA-hypertensive rats.
the angiotension II system is overactive in the anterior hypothalamus of the DOCA-salt rat.
angiotensin-II type 1 receptor antagonism in the AHA lowers blood pressure in hypertensive rats.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
brain angiotensins in the AHA are involved in the maintenance and development of hypertension in DOA-salt hypertensive rat.

the enhanced angiotensinsystem activity in the AHA contributes, at least in part, to the maintenance of hypertension, and that the enhanced angio-tensinsystem activity is caused by increased pressor re-activity to angiotension II and increased releaseof angiotensin.
the brain angiotensins and the renin-angiotensin-system (RAS) play an important role in the regulation of blood pressure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the angioten-sin-system is enhanced in the AHA in DOCA-salted hypertensive rats.
